claim: AITL is the most common subtype of PTCL (21–36.1%)
source: Except for PTCL-NOS, AITL is the most common subtype of PTCL (21–36.1%) (Chiba and Sakata-Yanagimoto, 2020; de Leval et al., 2015)
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature

claim: AITL is believed to arise from a subset of peripheral mature CD4+ T-cells corresponding to T-follicular helper (TFH) cells
source: AITL is the most common subtype of PTCL (21–36.1%) (Chiba and Sakata-Yanagimoto, 2020; de Leval et al., 2015) and is believed to arise from a subset of peripheral mature CD4+ T-cells corresponding to T-follicular helper (TFH) cells, characterized immunophenotypically by expression of a set of cellular markers like PD1, CXCR5, BCL-6, CD10, CXCL13, and ICOS-1 (Attygalle et al., 2002; Chiba and Sakata-Yanagimoto, 2020; Dupuis et al., 2006; Marafioti et al., 2010; Mourad et al., 2008)
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: TFH cells are characterized immunophenotypically by expression of PD1, CXCR5, BCL-6, CD10, CXCL13, and ICOS-1
source: characterized immunophenotypically by expression of a set of cellular markers like PD1, CXCR5, BCL-6, CD10, CXCL13, and ICOS-1 (Attygalle et al., 2002; Chiba and Sakata-Yanagimoto, 2020; Dupuis et al., 2006; Marafioti et al., 2010; Mourad et al., 2008)
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature

claim: AITL has low estimated rates of overall and failure-free survival at 5 years (33% and 18%, respectively)

evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: AITL is characterized by genomic mutations in TET2, RHOA, DNMT3A, and IDH2
source: Genetically, AITL is characterized by a number of genomic mutations in TET2, RHOA, DNMT3A, and IDH2 (Fiore et al., 2020a; Nakamoto-Matsubara et al., 2014; Odejide et al., 2014; Sakata-Yanagimoto et al., 2014; Yoo et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature

claim: TET2 and DNMT3A are frequently associated with myeloid malignancies, including AML, MPN, and MDS/MPN

evidence: Draws from established scientific knowledge

claim: TET2 and DNMT3A are the most commonly mutated genes associated with clonal hematopoiesis (CH) in healthy adults, especially those over 60 years of age
source: TET2 and DNMT3A are also the most commonly mutated genes associated with clonal hematopoiesis (CH) in healthy adults, especially those over 60 years of age
evidence: Draws from established scientific knowledge

claim: CH is an aging-related process characterized by clonal expansion of hematopoietic cells harboring one or more somatic mutations
source: CH has been shown to be an aging-related process characterized by the clonal expansion of hematopoietic cells harboring one or more somatic mutations as a result of selective advantage in the hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells due to enhanced self-renewal and inhibition of differentiation (Challen and Goodell, 2020; Gondek and DeZern, 2020; Jaiswal and Ebert, 2019; Steensma and Ebert, 2020)
